newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends up on Sparks number, wet weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends up on Sparks number, wet weather.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed higher on bullish input from an acreage estimate from Memphis-based analytical firm Sparks Companies and on concerns about excessive wet weather in portions of the U.S. Midwest, traders said.
Another surge in soybean futures also contributed to gains in corn.
Traders said Sparks pegged 1997 U.S. corn acreage at 80.8 million, slightly below USDA's working number of 81 million and below the firm's previous estimate for 81.5 million.
But the market remained tentative about that acreage forecast as concerns about excessive wet weather in the U.S. Midwest could cause a shift away from corn plantings into soybean seedings.
That possibility was triggering December corn/November soybean spreading.

"A lot of the buying in corn is in the December. It's normal this time of year for funds to go long new crop before spring planting and potential weather problems," said Paul Haugens, vice president of Chicago-based FIMAT Futures.
Corn closed 1-1/2 to 6-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with March up 6-1/2 at $3.07-1/4 a bushel.
Meteorologists early Friday said more rain fell in the already-waterlogged Ohio River Valley and more than a foot of snow fell from the Dakotas to Wisconsin.
"That is a lot of rain where they don't need it," said Fred Gesser, meteorologist with Weather Express Inc.

Refco Inc bought six million bushels of May, three million December and two million July, traders said. Refco also sold four million bushels of May, they said. FIMAT Futures bought five million bushels of December and Cargill Inc bought three million bushels of May, floor sources said.
Chartists said the four- and 20-day moving averages for the March were giving off bullish signals.
The short term nine-day relative strength index (RSI) for the March closed at 55 percent. The market considers an RSI of 70 or more as overbought and 30 or less as oversold.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 100,000 contracts, above the 98,823 traded Thursday.
In corn options, Lind Waldock bought 1,000 July $2.90 puts and sold 1,000 July $3.40 calls at three cents and FIMAT Futures sold 800 May $3.00 puts at 8-1/2 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 26,000 contracts, above the 17,020 traded Thursday.
